29148.etyen:
Compound of Latin cēpa (“onion”) + løk (“onion”), with the first element adapted as kepa-, literally “onion-onion”.
The Latin element is also found as caepa, possibly from an Anatolian source, but its further origin is unknown. The second element, løk (“onion”), derives from Old Norse laukr (“leek, onion, garlic”), from Proto-Norse ᛚᚨᚢᚲᚨᛉ (laukaʀ, “leek”), from Proto-Germanic *laukaz (“leek, onion”); its further origin is uncertain.
Compare the parallel formations Norwegian Nynorsk kepalauk and kepaløk, Danish kepaløg and Swedish kepalök (“onion”).

en.g: a female given name from Latin [in turn from Ancient Greek, in turn from Biblical Hebrew], equivalent to English Anna
x: Anina kommer på besøk i morgen.
Anina is coming to visit tomorrow.
3. Vara Emmelin Anina Sæter Bendiksen, 7.klasse, Kongsvik skole
Third alternate: Emmelin Anina Sæter Bendiksen, seventh grade, Kongsvik School.

1004252.etyen:
The immediate formation of the given name is uncertain. Store norske leksikon describes Anina as possibly derived from one of the female given names Anna, Anne or Ane. Nordic Names instead analyses it as a Romance diminutive of Anna, formed with the diminutive suffix -ina after a stem ending in -n.
The name ultimately belongs to the Anna name family, from Late Latin Anna (“female given name”), from Koine Greek Ἄννα (Ánna, “Anna”), from Biblical Hebrew חַנָּה (Ḥannāh, “Hannah; grace, favour”).
Compare Danish Anina and Swedish Anina (“female given name”).

1004764.etyen:

1005020.etyen:
Compound of mur (“masonry wall, foundation wall”) + svill (“sill, wall plate”), literally “wall sill”.
The first element mur (“masonry wall”) is from Old Norse múrr (“wall”), borrowed through Old English mūr (“wall”) or Old Saxon mūr (“wall”) from Latin mūrus (“wall”), from Proto-Italic *moiros (“wall”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mey- (“to fix, build fortifications or fences”).
The second element svill (“sill, wall plate”) is inherited through Middle Norwegian svill (“sill”) from Old Norse syll (“sill”), from Proto-Germanic *swellijō (“sill, wooden foundation beam”), of uncertain de
